body:
From the terms_enum design docs:

>we do not plan to support Document-Level-Security or other forms of doc-level filtering

The issue with the new (fast) implementation is that it relies on quickly reading terms directly from Lucene's alphabetically sorted index without checking if the docs that contain those terms are accessible to the end user. Based on this "unfiltered" assumption, things like document-level security or filters associated with aliases can't be supported and no results are returned in these scenarios.

rename.to: _terms_enum not supporting fields by alias for non-super user

body:
Fundamentally the terms_enum API relies on how the security framework behaves. 

>when called with an alias, seems to check the user's privs first on that alias, and then also on the index.

I do recall the security team contemplating dropping aliases at one point due to the potential for conflicting rules on aliases and underlying indices. This may be an example. The TermsEnum api implementation calls the security framework for targeted indices and only if the security framework returns with the response that _all_ documents are accessible will it then attempt to return field value suggestions.
I can take a closer look tomorrow.

Just wanted to add a follow-up here:

I've configured an index alias that points to specific indices. I created a role that has access to the alias (but not the underlying indices themselves).

I am able to do a terms aggregation against the alias and get results, but when I try to do a `_terms_enum` call to that alias, no results are returned.

Just wanted to clarify the issue here 😄

>I am able to do a terms aggregation against the alias and get results, but when I try to do a _terms_enum call to that alias, no results are returned.

Incidentally, note that this is the expected behaviour if you happen to have DLS enabled on an index - aggs will work, terms_enum will not. Regardless of any aliases. I'm not saying that DLS rules are behind this issue here - just a heads up.

I checked this out and it does appear to be a security discrepancy of the type that causes us to consider [removing support for security on aliases](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/29874) (still an open issue I see).

The terms enum API has aliases resolved into index names on the coordinating node and does additional access checks on data nodes using the index names. These fail for the same reason that `GET my_alias/_search` works and `GET my_index/_search` fails if the user is granted access to an index via an alias. I added some [comments](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/29874) to that issue to solicit opinion on if this is something we should support and fix. See also the comment there on false positives for any alias filters.
